questions.question: What is long polling?

options.text: A technique where the client makes a request and the server holds it open until new data is available

questions.explanation: Long polling: client requests, server waits (holds connection) until data available or timeout. Then responds, client immediately re-requests. Simulates push over HTTP. Works through proxies, firewalls.

questions.question: What is WebSocket?

options.text: A protocol providing full-duplex communication over a single persistent TCP connection

questions.explanation: WebSocket: persistent, bidirectional connection. Starts as HTTP upgrade, then raw TCP frames. Both client and server can send anytime. Low overhead after handshake. Ideal for: chat, gaming, live updates.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of WebSockets over long polling?

options.text: Lower latency and overhead—no repeated connection setup, true bidirectional communication

questions.explanation: WebSocket advantages: single connection (no reconnection overhead), true bidirectional (server pushes anytime), lower latency (no HTTP headers per message), efficient for high-frequency updates.

questions.question: When would you choose long polling over WebSockets?

options.text: When you need to work through restrictive proxies/firewalls or have infrequent updates

questions.explanation: Long polling advantages: works through HTTP proxies (WebSocket may be blocked), simpler server implementation, stateless (easier scaling), sufficient for infrequent updates. Corporate networks often block WebSocket.

questions.question: What is the connection overhead difference between long polling and WebSockets?

options.text: Long polling: new HTTP connection per update; WebSocket: single persistent connection

questions.explanation: Overhead comparison: Long polling = HTTP headers (~800 bytes) per request/response cycle. WebSocket = 2-14 bytes per frame after handshake. For frequent messages, WebSocket dramatically more efficient.

questions.question: How does server scalability differ between long polling and WebSockets?

options.text: Long polling: stateless, easier horizontal scaling; WebSocket: stateful connections require sticky sessions or pub/sub

questions.explanation: Scaling differences: Long polling = stateless, any server can respond, easy load balancing. WebSocket = stateful connection, need sticky sessions or pub/sub (Redis) to broadcast across servers. More complex.

questions.question: What happens when a WebSocket connection drops?

options.text: Client must detect and manually reconnect, potentially missing messages during disconnect

questions.explanation: WebSocket disconnect: client must detect (heartbeat/ping-pong), reconnect manually. Messages during disconnect lost unless: server queues, client requests replay. Libraries like Socket.IO handle reconnection automatically.

questions.question: What is Server-Sent Events (SSE) and how does it compare?

options.text: HTTP-based server-to-client push—simpler than WebSocket but unidirectional

questions.explanation: SSE: HTTP-based, server pushes to client. Unidirectional (server → client only). Auto-reconnection built-in. Works through proxies. Simpler than WebSocket. Good for: news feeds, notifications. Not for: chat, gaming.

questions.question: What is the latency difference between long polling and WebSockets?

options.text: WebSocket: near-instant delivery; Long polling: up to timeout duration delay

questions.explanation: Latency: WebSocket = message sent immediately over open connection. Long polling = if request just started, instant; if request about to timeout, must wait for new request. Variable latency.

questions.question: How do mobile apps typically handle real-time updates?

options.text: WebSocket when connected, with push notifications for background and reconnection handling

questions.explanation: Mobile real-time: WebSocket when app active (low latency). Push notifications (APNs, FCM) when backgrounded. Handle: reconnection on network change, battery optimization. Libraries: Socket.IO, Pusher handle complexity.

questions.question: What is Socket.IO?

options.text: A library that provides WebSocket-like API with fallbacks to long polling and automatic reconnection

questions.explanation: Socket.IO: abstraction layer. Uses WebSocket when available, falls back to long polling. Features: auto-reconnection, rooms/namespaces, acknowledgments, binary support. Simplifies real-time development.

questions.question: You're building a stock trading dashboard with price updates every 100ms. Which technology?

options.text: WebSocket—low latency, efficient for high-frequency updates

questions.explanation: High-frequency updates (100ms) = WebSocket. Long polling overhead too high (HTTP headers per update). WebSocket: minimal frame overhead, persistent connection, sub-millisecond delivery. Essential for trading, gaming.
